 Dongfeng Nissan opens orders for NX7 plug-in hybrid with up to 198 miles of electric range
 Saturday, 14 November 2026, 23:28 
 Photo source: Electrek 
 The NX7 is listed at 129,900 yuan, or about $19,400, and is advertised with up to 320 km (about 198 miles) of all-electric range. 
 Dongfeng Nissan opened early orders for the NX7 on November 13. The announcement refers to a 40 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery, while the detailed powertrain description gives its capacity as 40.9 kWh.
 This is reported by Electrek .
 The crossover has a 1.5-liter naturally aspirated engine rated at 98 hp, paired with a 228 hp electric motor. It is not immediately clear whether the NX7 uses a conventional parallel hybrid system or a series-hybrid setup with a plug. Dongfeng’s hybrid technology patents describe four possible operating modes: series hybrid, parallel hybrid, direct engine drive and electricity generation. Whether some or all of these modes will be used in the production NX7 remains unclear.
 Advertisement 
 A fully charged and fueled NX7 can travel 1,666 km (about 1,035 miles). Whether any or all of the patent-described operating modes will make it into the production NX7 remains to be seen.
 The NX7 is about the same length as a Tesla Model Y. Its interior includes a 17.3-inch central touchscreen and a fully digital instrument cluster. Higher-spec versions add a 55-inch augmented-reality head-up display powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P automotive processor. The vehicle runs Nissan OS 3.0 and has an AI voice assistant developed with iFlytek. Nissan says the assistant can understand natural-language commands, remember user preferences and recognize occupants to adjust vehicle settings.
 Top-spec models have “AI Zero-Pressure Cloud Blanket” seats, with sensors and air cushions that adjust dynamically. The seats include heating, ventilation and a 12-point massage function. The front seats can recline into a bed-like configuration. The NX7 also has an onboard refrigerator and a motion-sickness prevention system that Nissan claims can reduce motion sickness by up to 83%.
 The production version is due to be shown publicly for the first time at the Guangzhou Auto Show later in November.
